findings.text: During the 1920s, several scientists—including **Louis de Broglie, Werner Heisenberg, Erwin Schrödinger, Max Born**, and others—developed quantum mechanics.

Dalton's claim that all atoms of one element are identical in mass is not literally true. Isotopes have the same proton number—and are therefore the same element—but different neutron numbers and mass
Experiments with cathode rays led **J. J. Thomson** in 1897 to identify a universal negatively charged constituent of atoms: the electron. This demonstrated that atoms were divisible.
